outcome: No result addressing whether the Henson graphs have the finite model property was found; the question remains open as of September 2026.
summary: The question 'Do the Henson graphs have the finite model property?' is a decidability-flavored model-theoretic question about the Henson graphs (the countable homogeneous universal K_i-free graphs) that is distinct from other actively studied properties of these structures. I searched broadly for any work addressing this specific question and found none. There has been substantial, active research on Henson graphs in the window (26 Jan 2024–present), but all of it targets different questions: finite big Ramsey degrees (Dobrinen's 2023 result and its 2026 follow-ups, e.g. 'The finite big Ramsey degrees of Henson graphs are provable in ACA_0', arXiv 2606.30885, and 'The Henson graphs: colorings and codings' by Cholak, Dobrinen and McCoy, arXiv 2604.09894, submitted April 2026), indivisibility and computable indivisibility ('A note on the indivisibility of the Henson graphs', arXiv 2310.20097, which itself predates the frozen revision, from October 2023), and a separate, differently-named 'finite length property' (an algebraic/automata-theoretic notion about equivariant subspace chains, unrelated in substance to the logical finite model property) proved for the Rado graph and various Fraisse limits in 'The Finite Length Property of the Rado Graph and Friends' (Yang, Bojanczyk, Klin; arXiv 2605.21681) -- this paper explicitly does not mention Henson graphs or the finite model property, and 'finite length property' is a different concept despite the similar name (a trap worth flagging: it is easy to conflate the two on a keyword search). None of these results bears on whether every sentence true in some model of the Henson graphs' theory is true in some finite model (or on the decidability of the class via finite models). The Henson graph's own Wikipedia article still states the question as an unresolved 'unsolved problem in mathematics' box, and its edit history shows only a March 2025 edit that added the unsolved-problem template (no change to the underlying claim) and later cosmetic disputes about illustrative figures -- nothing bearing on the mathematical content. I was unable to fully load one general survey on Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures (par.nsf.gov, connection reset) that might discuss open problems in this area, but multiple other searches and the current article state converge on the same conclusion: no progress has been made on this specific question in the window. No AI involvement of any kind was found, since no result on this question was found at all.
competing_reading: One could argue that the finite big Ramsey degree results (proving these degrees are provable in ACA_0, a comparatively weak subsystem) bear indirectly on the model-theoretic tractability of Henson graphs and thus are 'related' work worth counting as progress. But 'finite model property' is a specific technical notion (every satisfiable sentence in the relevant logic has a finite model) that these Ramsey-degree and reverse-mathematics results do not address, settle a case of, or move a bound on. They are a related-but-distinct research program per the scope rule in Section 3.1, not a case or partial result of this problem.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint explicitly proving or disproving that the (universal) theory of some/all Henson graphs G_i has the finite model property, or a survey/expert source stating that this specific question has been resolved, would settle it. Direct correspondence with model theorists working on homogeneous structures (e.g. Dobrinen, Konecny, or Braunfeld) could also confirm the status is unchanged.
